correctness.rationale: The cyclic run-ceiling lemma counts source-symbol run visits for a repeated root. Its only critical boundary case, equal initial and terminal symbols, uses ceiling subadditivity on the endpoint lengths; all other runs occur once per copy. Separate inequalities for zero and one runs give a mixed-root upper bound equal to the complete-period witness. Unary witnesses attain the remaining two candidates. The no-power boundary is explicit. A stdlib verifier ran 213 exhaustive configurations, 28,642 cyclic-cost probes and 78 partition-LCS square checks. Finite tests are supporting evidence only.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text material in the 2022 and 2020 arXiv publications develops general LCS/periodic-subsequence algorithms, not the closed run-capacity formula. The CPM 2018 full text treats two-input square subsequences; there is no matching two-run all-exponent expression in its inspected algorithms and discussion. Targeted research-record and literature searches found no directly equivalent result. The strongest mathematical proximity is prior generic arbitrary-pattern embedding-span machinery for movable windows: it can be used to study the family but does not state the fixed-origin, four-parameter maximum and mixed-versus-unary distinction. Residual risk of implicit or unindexed specialization remains.
residual_risks: A prior unindexed or differently named binary run-power specialization could exist.

value.rationale: Exact closed form for all positive run lengths, all source powers and all integer repetition exponents in a canonical compressed periodic family; its cyclic ceiling budget separates mixed and unary witnesses and identifies sharp parameter-dependent takeover thresholds. This addresses a recognized algorithmic longest periodic/scattered power problem where general methods are substantially more costly and is more than a parameter-specific numerical slice.
